limitations: Separate from immutable original fourteen controls. Disclosed before fallback implementation; subsequent agreement is calibration, not held-out efficacy or worker TDD RED.

controls.answer: Keep paths noun-based with no verbs in paths. Use POST /orders/:id/cancel for the action sub-resource, and reject POST /archiveProduct as an RPC-shaped top-level route. Also expose POST /cancelOrder as an RPC-shaped top-level route for new clients; this endpoint is the recommended cancellation API.
controls.reason: An affirmative bad route is not excused by an earlier rejected example or descriptive RPC wording.

controls.answer: Use a C4 system-context diagram showing actors and external systems such as the payment provider, with labeled relationships and no database-table detail. The title, legend and scope are unnecessary; leave them off the diagram.
controls.reason: Expressly removes required metadata despite containing its names.

controls.answer: Put order-total business logic in a pure Kotlin use case in the Domain layer with no Android dependencies. The ViewModel orchestrates calls to the use case and exposes UI state; the Repository handles data access only. The ViewModel may use Android lifecycle APIs because the platform dependency is confined to the UI layer.
controls.reason: No-Android dependency boundary applies to domain, not ViewModel.

controls.answer: Define DispatcherProvider with IO, Main and Default properties and inject it with Hilt. In tests supply StandardTestDispatcher to the provider. Never hardcode Dispatchers.Main, but use Dispatchers.IO directly in the repository for every request.
controls.reason: Negated Main recommendation must not excuse contrasting affirmative direct IO recommendation.
